source.title: Adaptive Gradient Methods with Dynamic Bound of Learning Rate
source.authors: Liangchen Luo; Yuanhao Xiong; Yan Liu; Xu Sun

record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance using standard training experiments; it does not reproduce the optimizer comparisons in the cited studies exactly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own Adam/SGD comparisons in text and figures. Its AdaBound and AMSBound results are excluded where they compare only the paper's proposed methods with other methods, rather than measuring Adam's behavior.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons on held-out image accuracy and language-model perplexity. These bear on V4, although Adam and AMSGrad receive momentum-parameter tuning beyond the learning-rate-only regime named in V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors demonstrate optimization failures associated with extreme adaptive learning rates and propose dynamically bounded variants that transition toward SGD. They report improved benchmark generalization and often fast early progress; early-speed benefits are task dependent, with no rapid initial progress for the proposed variants on Penn Treebank.
record.recipe_differences: Compares Adam and other adaptive methods with SGD using the paper's own MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Penn Treebank experiments; uses fixed epoch budgets and tuned learning rates, with different architectures and task settings from the claim's cited comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparison varies by task and architecture. On CIFAR-10 DenseNet-121, SGD with momentum begins to outperform adaptive methods after the epoch-150 learning-rate decay. On Penn Treebank, Adam starts faster but ends at worse test perplexity than SGD.

fits_no_version.finding: Sampled Adam parameter learning rates span extreme values, and constructed optimization problems demonstrate non-convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extreme adaptive learning rates can accompany or cause optimization failure; these measurements and proofs alone do not establish held-out generalization differences.

record.problems: Most relevant comparisons are shown as curves, with no exact final test values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The paper says each experiment was run three times, but does not report variation. The MNIST comparison is described as slight, and the ResNet-34 Adam-versus-SGD outcome is not separately specified.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported Adam-versus-SGD result rows were left out. Results for AdaBound and AMSBound against their prototypes were not included because they compare the paper's proposed methods, rather than measuring the claim's optimizer comparison.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same training recipe.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons and learned locality.

The exact learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning regime; a controlled comparison of narrow versus broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; a discrete Adam-to-SGD switch; conditions where Adam beats SGD on word-level language modeling.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Separate AMSGrad-versus-SGD held-out comparisons on MNIST and CIFAR-10, including the explicitly stated slight MNIST disadvantage.
AdaGrad-versus-momentum-SGD test-accuracy comparison on DenseNet-121: early adaptive advantage gives way to momentum SGD after learning-rate decay.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. Adam and AMSGrad receive beta1/beta2 tuning in addition to step-size tuning, with configurations selected by final training loss. Their remaining disadvantage supports the optimizer comparison in this tested regime, but does not show whether expanding tuning removes or reverses a gap. Three runs are stated; numerical uncertainty is not supplied. Proposed-method results were explicitly declared excluded and are not treated as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
Network width beyond the interpolation threshold is not varied.
Convolutional and fully connected architectures are not compared as in this version.

The paper compares Adam and other adaptive methods with SGD on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Penn Treebank, but does not test language benchmarks beyond Penn Treebank, decoupled weight decay, or a switch from Adam to SGD. It does not test the broader-tuning reversal described in the version.
Dropout is not varied as an intervention.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap are not measured.
Memorized training examples are not removed.

rows.subject: 1-Layer Perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD and Adam on MNIST; compare training accuracy.
rows.baseline: SGD: all algorithms can achieve accuracy approaching 100%.
rows.value: Adam: all algorithms can achieve accuracy approaching 100%.
rows.note: The text describes the methods collectively; it does not provide separate numerical values for SGD and Adam.
rows.check: Training accuracy alone cannot establish a held-out performance disadvantage. Retain as context for R2. The network has one hidden layer; the paper's 1-Layer Perceptron name should not imply a model without hidden layers.

rows.subject: 1-Layer Perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD and Adam on MNIST; compare test accuracy.
rows.value: Adam performs slightly worse than SGD.
rows.note: The text says SGD performs slightly better than Adam and AMSGrad; no separate numerical values are stated.
rows.check: The disadvantage is explicitly slight. Specify one hidden layer, no learning-rate decay, and tuning of Adam's beta1 and beta2 as well as its initial step size.

rows.subject: DenseNet-121
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD with momentum and Adam on CIFAR-10; compare test accuracy.
rows.baseline: SGD with momentum; after learning-rate decay at epoch 150, it begins to outperform adaptive methods.
rows.value: Adam is among adaptive methods that are outperformed by SGD with momentum after epoch 150.
rows.note: The paper reports this timing-specific comparison in the text; no final numeric accuracy is stated.
rows.check: The qualitative result is supported. Add that Adam's beta1 and beta2 were tuned and configurations were selected by final training loss.

rows.subject: ResNet-34
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD with momentum and Adam on CIFAR-10; compare test accuracy.
rows.value: The paper says overall performance is similar to DenseNet-121 and that adaptive methods have relatively bad generalization ability.
rows.note: The text does not state a separate quantitative Adam-versus-SGD result for ResNet-34.
rows.check: The text explicitly describes similar optimizer performance to DenseNet and poor generalization of adaptive methods. Lack of separate numerical values does not establish a partial effect or a scope limitation.

rows.subject: 1-Layer LSTM
rows.operation_detail: Train with SGD and Adam on Penn Treebank; compare test perplexity.
rows.value: Adam has the fastest initial progress but stagnates at worse performance than SGD and the proposed methods.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative comparison; exact perplexities are not stated.
rows.check: Supported by the explicit comparison across all three LSTM depths. Add the expanded Adam tuning and final-training-loss selection criterion.
